Distribution. The species is a Mexican endemic in the Atlantic plains east from the Sierra Madre Oriental, from the states of Nuevo León and Tamaulipas to Oaxaca and Veracruz (Fig. 15, black circles). From a biogeographic perspective, the species is characteristic of the Mexican Transition Zone and the Caribbean Mesoamerican domain.

Distribution: Neotropical: Brazil. Host: Moraceae: Cecropia adenopus, Cecropia sp. New Record: Brazil, G. Bondar on Cecropia sp., 1 slide with 7 puparia in USNM. Comment: The USNM has one slide of this species with 7 puparia that is marked as a cotype. The area surrounding the vasiform orifice is very dark and sclerotized and difficult to observe in the USNM specimens. However, one individual is lighter and shows the vasiform orifice is set on top of a large, volcano-like protuberance, which we have not observed in other whitefly species. Carapia-Ruiz (2020 b) reported and provided a photograph of this species found on Curatella americana and Psidium guajava in Mexico.
